John Hickenlooper

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Colorado · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from Colorado

John Hickenlooper is the Democratic U.S. senator from Colorado. He is running for a second term, which he has said would be his last. Before joining the Senate he was Denver's mayor and then Colorado's governor, and he won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary against state Sen. Julie Gonzales.

Where Hickenlooper stands

Health care / Medicaid
Says health care should be a right and not a privilege, and supports universal coverage. Opposes the Medicaid cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill, saying they put rural Colorado hospitals and clinics at risk of closing.
Immigration enforcement
Says ICE is operating like a "secret police force." Says he would consider a lawsuit if the GEO Group detention center in Aurora does not let state and county health officials inspect it.
Legal immigration
Says the U.S. provides enough legal pathways for people to immigrate, but argues those pathways are being dismantled and ignored by the current administration.
Fuel prices
Supports temporarily suspending federal gas and diesel taxes. Opposes the administration's deal to buy diesel from Russia, saying Russia would use the money to attack Ukraine.
Social Security
Says Social Security's solvency cannot wait decades for investment-account solutions, and says higher earners should pay more into the system.
Iran
Opposes the war in Iran and has called it illegal.
Trump administration
Lists "Stopping the Trump Administration's Lawlessness" as the top priority on his campaign website. Says he regrets the confirmation of every Trump Cabinet member he voted for.
Climate / energy
Criticized the EPA's proposed rollback of federal methane rules for oil and gas operations, saying it will allow more pollutants into the air.
Term limits
Has said that if he is re-elected in 2026, it will be his last Senate term. He called the pledge an "oath of conscience."

Background

  • Mayor of Denver (elected 2003)
  • Governor of Colorado (former)
  • U.S. Senator from Colorado (current; first term)
  • Won the 2026 Democratic primary with 52.8% of the vote over Julie Gonzales
  • Attended college in Middletown, Connecticut (Wesleyan University)
